title.narrative: Local Government Capacity Building Grant to Implement Intergovernmental Fiscal Reforms

description.narrative: The main objective of this multi-year (2 year) project is to build capacity at regional/local government levels to successfully implement intergovernmental fiscal reforms outlined in the proposed PRSG (Poverty Reduction Strategy Grant) for Kyrgyz Republic. The recent National Poverty Reduction Strategy (NPRS) and the proposed PRSG refer to Kyrgyz government's intention to further decentralize decision-making and public services to the local levels. These new reforms will entail a significant increase in subnational governments' responsibilities (ex: local self-governments, LSGs), especially in areas such as managing expenditure; improving local revenue capacity; streamlining the work programs of local treasuries to better align with the fiscal reforms proposed; and promoting effective and transparent service delivery at local levels. With their current skill profiles and weak capacity, a vast majority of local self-governments in Kyrgyz Republic are unlikley to be able to undertake these responsibilities, thus posing a serious challenge to the full and successful implementation of proposed IGF reforms. This also means that there is a critical need for a significant and strcutured capacity building program to address the evolving needs over time. The Ministry of Local Self-Government (MLSG) estimates that a minimum of 1000 staff from LSGs - including key staff members in finance departsments of Aiyl Okmatus, Oblasts/Raiyons -should be trained in areas of budget formulation, procurement, and intergovernmental finance, within the next few years. This critical mass of officials at LSGs should be in place prior to the full implementation of PRSG in order to guarantee the success of reforms. The proposed IDF grant outlines a program which will strengthen the capacity of LSGs to implement the reforms. The purpose of the Grant is to assist the Recipient in capacity building at regional and local government levels to successfully implement intergovernmental fiscal reforms (IGFs), help strengthen accountability mechanisms in the local budget process and build a strong and viable coalitions between officials in regional financial departments and local governments with a clear enunciation of revenue and expenditure responsibilities of each level of government.
